children: JD Sports Fashion's results could trigger a positive reaction given low expectations, analysts at Bernstein say. The British retailer reported sales of 2.91 billion pounds for its third quarter through October, down 2.6% on year on a like-for-like basis. The performance was better than expected in North America, the U.K. and Europe, but still soft, the analysts write in a research note. The company narrowed its profit before tax and adjusted items guidance to a range of 700 million pounds to 750 million pounds. Consensus is already at the midpoint of the range, so the numbers shouldn't move too much, they add. (andrea.figueras@wsj.com)
